title: Sheep’s Intestines
paragraphs: “So this is money earned through labor, huh?”
Father muttered as he gazed at the earnings from the Adventurers’ Guild.
“Naofumi, didn’t you have a part-time job before?”
“Working in Japan and working in another world are completely different.”
“That’s true.”
“It feels different from the financial aid from the kingdom or the money Motoyasu gave me.”
“Hmm… Looking at this alone, you all seem just like rookie adventurers.”
Éclair folded her arms and murmured, to which Father responded, looking slightly embarrassed.
“Well, our levels might be decent, but we still lack experience. There are a lot of things we’re doing for the first time—it can’t be helped.”
“Exactly.”
“We’re no different from beginner adventurers. Do you even realize how few days it’s been since we were summoned?”

Each of them protested to Éclair in turn. Though it didn’t seem like she was entirely serious about what she said, so there was no real problem. Meanwhile, I turned my gaze—and the money in my hand—toward Yuki and the others.
“Alright! Time for an allowance! Yuki, you guys, let’s go eat to our hearts’ content at the food stalls!”
“Yaaay!”
With that, I grabbed Yuki and the others and dashed off to the marketplace.
“Motoyasu is way too carefree.”
“Even Sakura… Well, I suppose it can’t be helped.”
“Shall we get something to tide us over until Naofumi’s cooking is ready?”
“So it’s just expected at this point that I’ll cook at least one meal a day, and no one even questions it anymore…?”
And so, another day passed with the Heroes strangely getting along well. That evening, Father prepared hamburg steaks and a meatball hot pot for dinner.
“Eat as much as you like!”
“Naofumi… Just how good at cooking are you?”
Ren asked while eating a hamburger steak.
“Where did you even get the ground meat?”
“I chopped it up with a knife. It was kind of a hassle.”
Even now, Father was skillfully mincing meat with his knife.
Was he making something different from the hamburg steaks?
“Shall I help?”
“Just don’t try mincing meat by slamming it with your spear, okay? There’s a proper way to do things.”
“Understood!”
Under Father’s guidance, I joined in to help with the cooking. I focused entirely on chopping the meat with a knife.
“This tastes better than what I had at the castle. Iwatani-dono, you truly are skilled at cooking.”
“It’s delicious.”
“Sooo good!”
“Munch munch!”
“Alright, the hamburg steaks are done, and the hot pot is ready. Now then…”
Father was attaching a cap and a bag made from bones. He mixed ground meat with coarsely chopped smoked meat and put it inside.
What was he trying to make?
“I’m making something so we won’t have to worry about food for a while. Man, I’m really glad we found that sheep-type monster.”

As he spoke, he connected the cap to the sheep intestines he had instructed me to wash thoroughly earlier. He started pushing the ground meat through them, which had been mixed with herbs and antibacterial medicinal plants. I felt like I had seen this process somewhere before…
Then he twisted the stuffed intestine into sections… Oh! This was sausage! Ren and Itsuki were whispering to each other while watching the process.
“That guy is seriously weird.”
“How can someone make sausages in a survival situation like this?”
“At this point, he’s not the Shield Hero—he’s the Food Hero. Lately, even his shield looks like a cooking pot to me.”

“If he ever falls from being a hero and becomes a demon king, he’ll probably win over his subordinates by feeding them and making them swear loyalty through their stomachs. Bet that’s what he did in his previous world too.”
“You know, I can hear you two.”
Father pointed it out while continuing his work.
“Since I had to make these under these conditions, there’s a chance of failure. Food poisoning is scary, so being able to judge ingredients properly is essential… Poison detection too.”
“Didn’t Motoyasu use disinfectant? That’s how you cleaned the sheep intestines, right?”
“Well… yeah, but—okay, done.”
There were still plenty of ingredients left, but it looked like a good number of sausages had been completed.
Father also started making something thicker than a typical sausage… was this something else?
“Next, we need a kiln. Motoyasu, get the fire going.”
“On it!”
After having Éclair assemble the kiln, Father hung the sausages inside and began smoking them.
“We’ll take turns watching it to make sure the steam doesn’t escape… Sakura, use magic to help.”
“Okaaay!”
Sakura used magic to keep the smoke from leaking.
How convenient! Meanwhile, Father stuck skewers into the thicker sausages and started roasting them over an open flame.
“Alright, done. Homemade frankfurters… or something like that.”
Saying that, he handed them out to everyone. Ren and Itsuki, once again, started whispering to each other while watching him.
“I never expected to be eating a frankfurter in another world…”
“Even in a future with VR, they still exist?”
“Of course. You guys have them in your Japan with supernatural powers, don’t you?”
“Yeah. They taste great at festivals, but when you eat them at home, they’re kind of underwhelming.”
“Well, we’re eating these outside, and they’re made by Naofumi…”
“That makes them perfect…”
Such noisy people during a meal.
Good food should be eaten in silence, savoring every bite! Just like the Filolials!
“If you had to choose between Naofumi’s cooking or the luxurious cuisine of the country—”
“No contest. If we just let Naofumi eat it once, he’d replicate it perfectly. There’s no point in choosing.”

As I took a bite, the crisp skin burst open, releasing savory meat juices that spread across my tongue. The herbs added for seasoning not only stimulated the appetite but also provided a subtle, spicy kick. And the rich, smoky flavor of the coarsely ground smoked meat mixed in danced delightfully on my tongue.
“Maybe I’ll stir-fry some vegetables tomorrow? We’ve got a lot of extra meat.”
“Meat and vegetable stir-fry sounds good.”
“Can’t you make soup? Oh, and curry too.”
Ren and Itsuki each made their requests. That brought back memories.
Curry… I remember Father making it for his slaves in the first world.
“Curry, huh… We don’t have garam masala. Well, I guess I could make my own spices from scratch, but still…”
So it was difficult after all?
Then the solution was obvious—we just needed to find a place to procure the necessary seasonings! Father had been gathering seasonings, after all.
“Soup might be tricky. I can make something simple, but real broth takes time.”
“Just knowing how to make it is impressive enough!”
Ren’s dramatic point at Father was quite a sight to behold. A few days later… our journey by carriage continued.
“Gua!?”
“I heard the cry of a Filolial!”
A wild Filolial! I leaned out of the carriage and spotted a flock of Filolials in the distance. I quickly scanned the surroundings to see if there were more.
“Motoyasu really loves Filolials.”
“He sure does.”
“His love for Yuki and the others is one thing, but even after we reach Faubrey, he’s planning some sort of Filolial mass-production project.”
“Well, even just considering their strength, they’re undeniably a valuable force.”
“If the Waves are occurring worldwide… they might be worth serious consideration.”
“There’s the legend of the Divine Bird, but I don’t think it’s right for people to just rely on the Heroes and Filolials to handle the Waves while doing nothing themselves.”
“Agreed. Éclair makes a good point. I plan to involve the people of each country as well.”
“Filoliaaaal-samaaa!”
Since the Filolials were looking in our direction, I enthusiastically waved at them.
“Speeding up!”
Yuki, looking slightly annoyed, increased the pace.
Ah… the wild Filolials were getting further and further away. How disappointing.
“Waaait, Yuki!”
Kou started chasing after the carriage from behind. Meanwhile, inside the carriage, Sakura was snuggled up to Father, looking drowsy.
